blocked_arm_effects.label: NoInfo, Cuberoot, n in {1,4,7,10}: reserve price per additional bidder

compareAs.reason: mean of per-seller OLS slopes of the reserve on n: n is drawn independently of everything else and every seller has 60 periods, so it estimates the same within-seller slope as the random-intercept coefficient on n - nbar (the paper's model also has Per and Cube terms; Cube is constant within a seller)

estimates.variant: random-intercept regression on n - nbar and Per - Per, original data of this cell (replication report)

blocked_arm_effects.label: NoInfo (all four cells): reserve price per additional bidder (Model 1)

compareAs.reason: mean of per-seller OLS slopes of the reserve on n. This equals the pooled random-intercept coefficient on n - nbar only if every seller has the same slope (homogeneous slopes across bidder sets and distributions): the pooled model weights sellers by their n variance (about 1.25 for {1,2,3,4}, 11.25 for {1,4,7,10}) and also uses between-seller variation, while this estimand weights every seller equally. Figure 2 implies different slopes per set, so the level is not comparable; the engine offers no weighted per-seller slope, so this effect is scored on direction only (scoring, reference_mismatch)

estimates.variant: Table 2 Model (1): n - nbar, Per - Per, Cube; random effects for subjects

blocked_arm_effects.reference_mismatch: estimand mismatch: the printed coefficient is from a random-intercept model pooled over sellers with different n sets / distributions; the replay's unweighted mean of per-seller slopes matches it only under homogeneous slopes (fidelity review 1, R1-S2)
